standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-independence-characters (delivered card L48335; distinct characters are linearly independent), theorem-galois-theory (delivered card L48341; L^{Gal(L/K)} = K for a finite Galois extension), lemma-finite-Galois (|G| = [L : K] for finite Galois); linear algebra: a root of the minimal polynomial of an operator is an eigenvalue when the minimal polynomial splits with the root simple
core_obligations: For a generator sigma of Gal(L/K) = Z/nZ: sigma^n - 1 = 0 as a K-linear operator, and linear independence of the characters 1, sigma, ..., sigma^{n-1} forbids an annihilating polynomial of degree < n, so the minimal polynomial of sigma is x^n - 1

The primitive n-th root zeta is a root of x^n - 1, hence an eigenvalue of sigma: there is 0 != z in L with sigma(z) = zeta z; then sigma(z^n) = z^n so z^n in K (fixed-field part of theorem-galois-theory)
The orbit z, zeta z, ..., zeta^{n-1} z consists of n pairwise distinct K-conjugates of z, so [K(z) : K] >= n, while [L : K] = n; hence L = K[z] with z^n in K
proof_roadmap: Pin down the minimal polynomial of sigma by independence of characters
Extract an eigenvector for zeta and show z^n is fixed
Conclude generation by the distinct-orbit count
